question: Should imsg adopt `send-sticker` and `send.sticker` as a maintained advanced-bridge contract, and require recipient-visible exact-head proof before landing it?
rationale: Code inspection supports the guarded implementation, but only maintainers can accept the long-term private-framework support commitment and choose the end-to-end proof standard for this new public API.

options.title: Adopt after recipient proof
options.body: Accept the guarded API after redacted sender and recipient captures show standalone and exact-part attached sticker rendering on the exact head.

options.title: Accept current proof
options.body: Merge using local runtime and database evidence while explicitly owning recipient-rendering uncertainty and private-API compatibility.

options.title: Decline the API
options.body: Keep sticker metadata reading support but do not add a maintained private sticker-send surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt after recipient proof
recommendation.body: Accept the guarded API after redacted sender and recipient captures show standalone and exact-part attached sticker rendering on the exact head.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the hardening and final contract rewrite that defines the proposed long-term support boundary.
